newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives deny MPs resignation rumours.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives deny MPs resignation rumours.

text.p: UK Conservative party officials on Thursday denied financial market rumours that one or more of the ruling party's MPs had resigned from the parliamentary party in protest over the Government's policy on Europe.
The rumours reflect anger among Conservative "Euro-sceptics" over the government's refusal to permit a full-scale debate on the floor of Parliament over economic and monetary union.

One Euro-sceptic, former Treasury minister David Heathcoat-Amory, kept up pressure on the Government on Thursday by issuing a veiled threat against Prime Minister John Major, who has a majority of just one in the 651-seat House of Commons.

Referring to a defeat for the government in a key committee on Wednesday, the former minister told BBC radio: "A warning has been put out. We all want to support the government but only if the government looks after our freedoms."
Heathcoat-Amory said the government had made a mistake by insisting on debating aspects of the planned single currency in a specialist committee.

"It is time for the government to realise that this is a constitutional issue that goes to the core of what we are elected to do. It would be a great mistake if they persist in the belief that they cam somehow get all this through," he said.
The government is anxious to avoid a full-scale debate for fear of widening divisions in the Conservative party so close to the general election, which must be held by May 22.
